w:r.w:t: Cursor Prompt: E-Commerce Backend Final Project
Spring Boot Monolithic Backend • Java 21 • MySQL • JWT • Swagger
Use the following prompt in Cursor Agent/Composer. It tells Cursor to generate the complete backend project, following the same architecture as the previous Spring Boot Book Management project.
You are a senior Java Spring Boot backend engineer.
Create a complete monolithic backend for a students’ FINAL PROJECT.
- This is NOT a normal lesson project.
- This is a FINAL PROJECT backend.
- Students already have the frontend code and completed UI design.
- The frontend is an electronics e-commerce website with red/white styling.
- The frontend includes pages: Home, Sign Up, Log In, Shop, Cart, Checkout, Product Details, About, Contact, User Products, Create/Edit Product.
- The backend must provide REST APIs and be ready to connect to the existing frontend using fetch().
- Use the same backend style and structure as the previous Spring Boot Book Management project.

Generate a complete backend project that supports authentication, products, categories, cart, checkout/orders, contact messages, admin management, validation, exceptions, Swagger, JWT security, pagination, and filtering.
This must be one clean monolithic Spring Boot backend.
Follow this package and code architecture strictly:
Controller → Service Interface → Service Implementation → Repository → Entity
- USER can shop, use cart, checkout, and see own orders
- ADMIN can manage products, categories, orders, and contact messages
- Filter products by category, price range, and brand
- Product image is stored as String imageUrl for now
- Product GET APIs can be public
- Assign product to category through ProductRequest.categoryId
- Cannot add more than available stock
- If the same product is already in cart, increase quantity instead of creating duplicate cart item
- No real payment integration; simulate checkout
- My orders requires USER or ADMIN
- Cannot checkout if product stock is not enough
- Order total must be calculated from order items
- Use snapshot fields in OrderItem: productName, price, quantity
- Save contact message from Contact page
- Admin can view all contact messages
The frontend has User Products and Create/Edit Product pages.
- User Products page should show admin product list when logged in as ADMIN.
- Create/Edit Product page should call ADMIN product APIs.
- If a normal USER opens this page, backend must return 403 Forbidden.
Explain this in comments and documentation.
- OrderStatus with PENDING, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED
Use Lombok if configured, otherwise create constructors/getters/setters manually.
Use BigDecimal for prices, not double.
- filtering support using Specification or custom query
- Cart APIs require USER or ADMIN
- Extract Bearer token from Authorization header
- Allow frontend URL from application.properties, for example http://localhost:5500
- Allow GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS
Return clean JSON errors, not Java stack traces.
Swagger must support JWT Authorization button.

Add a documentation section or comments with fetch examples for major APIs.
20. frontend fetch examples in a README or comments
21. SQL/example data for admin, categories, products if useful

Normal user can be registered from frontend.
Make sure password is encrypted with BCrypt.
- User cannot login before email verification.
- Cart quantity must be at least 1.
- User cannot checkout if stock is not enough.
- OrderItem stores snapshot productName and price.
- Admin-only APIs must return 403 for normal users.
- Not found resources must return 404 with clean JSON.
- Validation errors must return 400 with field messages.
- Return clean DTOs, not raw entities
- Include comments where logic is important
